entities.summary:
Mathieu II, also known as Mathieu II, called the Great or the Great Constable, was a lord of Montmorency from 1189 and Constable of France from 1218 to 1230. 

He played a significant role in the governance of the French kingdom, particularly in the administration of justice and the collection of taxes. Mathieu II's tenure as Constable was marked by several key events, including the establishment of the Chamber of the Constable, which became a powerful institution in medieval France. 

His legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he contributed to the development of the French feudal system and the consolidation of the French monarchy. Mathieu II's influence can also be seen in the subsequent careers of his successors, who built upon his administrative reforms. 

The Mathieu II monument in the Château de Montmorency serves as a testament to his enduring presence in French history, and his name remains synonymous with the ideals of loyalty, duty, and service that defined the medieval nobility.
